title: 50agents vs Glide: AI app builders compared | 50agents
description: Glide builds internal apps from spreadsheets and prompts, $25 a month to publish; 50agents builds apps run by AI agents from plain words, free to start.
answer: Pick Glide if you want apps people install on their phones, public apps, or a Postgres connection your BI tools can read.
Pick 50agents if you want an internal app plus AI agents that work its records, and automations around it, from plain words; it is free to start.
ask: Track my leads and follow up
lede: Glide is the more complete app builder: apps start from a prompt, a PDF or a screenshot, can be public, and install on a phone.

us: You want AI agents doing work inside the app, such as following up each lead for your approval.
You want to use the app without paying to publish it.
The app is one piece of a job that also needs automations or a browser agent.
them: People outside your team need to use the app, or install it on their phones.
Your BI tools need to read the app's data directly.
You want to start from a PDF or a screenshot of the app you have in mind.

move.title: Export each table
move.body: Any table in a GlideOS project exports to CSV.

move.title: Ask for the app
move.body: Tell Captain what it is for, such as the ask at the top of this page. Captain asks which apps you use today before it plans.

move.title: Bring the data in
move.body: Drop the CSV into the app's list, and Captain matches the columns to the fields.

faqs.a: Glide has a free plan with limited credits and 10 projects, but 0 published apps and 0 enabled workflows. Basic is $25 a month.
No. They are for the people in your workspace. Glide can publish public apps from its Plus plan.
Glide says GlideOS works with more than 1,000 services; 50agents works with 2,300+ apps through viaSocket.
